title: Latest Savage on Security Webinar Focuses on Gen-AI for Chip Design and Security - Semiwiki
gist: The ESD Alliance is hosting a September 10, 2026 webinar where Warren Savage and Mark Tehranipoor will present a multi-agent LLM framework meant to unify SoC design synthesis, security threat modeling, and verification into one workflow.

themes.theme: Multi-Agent AI Framework for Chip Design & Security

themes.theme: Why Agentic AI in SoC Design

insights.claim: Traditional SoC design and verification methodologies are increasingly strained by escalating complexity, massive design scale, heterogeneous integration, and rapidly evolving security threats, exceeding the practical limits of conventional tool chains and human-centric workflows.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: This structural pain point is the underlying tailwind driving demand for LLM-based and agentic EDA tools.
insights.quote: Ensuring correctness, scalability, comprehensiveness and adaptability across the full SoC lifecycle now exceeds the practical limits of conventional tool chains and human-centric workflows.

insights.claim: LLMs are seen as enabling architectural reasoning, specification refinement, vulnerability analysis and design-space exploration in chip design beyond code generation, but monolithic models alone are viewed as insufficient, favoring an agentic paradigm of specialized collaborating agents.
insights.speaker: Admin
insights.so_what: Reinforces an industry view that multi-agent architectures, not single large models, are the likely winning approach for EDA workflows, relevant when evaluating EDA AI vendor roadmaps.
insights.quote: Monolithic models alone are insufficient for the multidisciplinary and iterative nature of chip design.
